summary: ONE additive, optional spec attribute: sink_config.export_trigger. It makes an AGGREGATING target (a materialized_view, or any TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD flow) exportable through a genuine Lakeflow sink for the first time. Nothing is removed; the default reproduces pre-1.7.5 behaviour exactly, so no existing spec changes shape or needs migrating.

added_attributes.description: WHAT drives the export. 'per_micro_batch' (default when absent) feeds the sink from the flow's own staged view: one archive per micro-batch of an append-only stream. 'per_update' decouples trigger from payload -- an update-scoped pulse drives the sink and the rows are read as a batch -- producing exactly ONE export per pipeline update, including an update that ingested no new rows.
added_attributes.why_it_exists: A Lakeflow sink is streaming-only, and Delta refuses to stream a fully-recomputed table (DELTA_SOURCE_TABLE_IGNORE_CHANGES; skipChangeCommits is refused framework-wide). Together those meant an aggregating target could be computed and published and then had no way to leave the platform as a file -- a structural contradiction, not a missing feature.
added_attributes.ui_action: Add a select 'Export trigger' to the sink editor, shown ONLY when sink_config.format is pgp_zip. Options: '' (unset = per_micro_batch), per_micro_batch, per_update. Hint under per_update: 'Use this when the flow AGGREGATES (GROUP BY / DISTINCT). Exactly one export per pipeline update, even if nothing was ingested.'
added_attributes.validation: Reject any value outside the enum. Presence-reject for format 'delta'/'kafka' (native Lakeflow sinks own their own write cadence) -- same contract as staged_file_format.
added_attributes.rejection_message_verbatim: target_config.sink_config.export_trigger: only meaningful for format 'pgp_zip' (this framework's staging-then-archive sink); format 'delta' is a native Lakeflow sink whose write cadence Lakeflow itself owns. Remove the attribute.
added_attributes.migration: None -- absent means 'per_micro_batch', the only pre-1.7.5 behaviour.

verification.regression_check: tests/unit diffed by failing-test-ID against a pre-change baseline: 125 vs 126 -- ZERO regressions, one pre-existing failure fixed. 255 passed across the five crypto/sink/spec suites. databricks-app 217/19/0 against a 208/19/0 baseline.
verification.live_runtime_verification: Pulse source chosen on evidence, not assumption. A side-by-side probe on the real serverless runtime fed two pulse variants into counting handlers: plain `rate` gave 1 row on a fresh checkpoint and 0 rows on the next incremental update (wall-clock dependent: rows = seconds since checkpoint creation); `rate-micro-batch` (rowsPerBatch=1) gave 1 row on both. The shipped pulse is rate-micro-batch. dlt.foreach_batch_sink was also confirmed present on this runtime, contradicting a code comment that refers to the local pip stub.
